column1: # Pointers in the data blob 0x00272c70-0x00494050. Addresses and names only.
# tier 1/2/3 = accepted (certain / strong / rule), x = rejected candidate (no value kept).

# Reasons: ftab: function start in a run of >=3 function-start words (callback/class/vtable tables); calltab: function start in a table code loads and calls through (jalr/jr); func: lone function start; jtbl: jump-table entry of an asm/unmatched function (analyze_asm); dma-chain: ADDR word of a DMA tag on a chain code kicks (sceDmaSend / D_TADR store), walked tag by tag; func-s16: function start, but the neighbourhood looks like s16 data (kept: starts are rare by chance); dref: target is an address code builds with %hi/%lo (or a D_ name src references), not s16/colour-like; ptab: word in a table/variable code loads and dereferences or calls through; dma: ADDR word of a valid REF/REFS/REFE/NEXT/CALL tag (payload VIF/GIF, in range) in a tag table code references (templates code copies into packets); str: points at the start of a NUL-terminated string; stride: same offset as accepted pointers in a repeating record (stride 8-64, both sides); bref: bss target code builds with %hi/%lo; typed: tier-3 word inside a pointer variable/array a src extern declares (T *D_x, T *D_x[n], (*D_x[n])()); override: accepted by a reviewed entry of tools/shift/data_reloc_overrides.tsv (typed evidence, reason there); dptr-run: aligned data target next to other pointer words with different values or accepted pointers; bptr-run: aligned bss target next to other pointer words with different values or accepted pointers; dptr: aligned data target, isolated, no rule against it (the real ambiguous remainder); bptr: aligned bss target, isolated, no rule against it (the real ambiguous remainder); near: aligned target within 64 KiB of the word itself (self-relative records, lists), not s16-like; mirror: 0x20000000/0x30000000 mirror of a 16-aligned data/bss address code builds with %hi/%lo; into-table: inside an asm/unmatched function, next to other words into it, distinct, not s16-like; typed-x: tier-3 word inside an s16/u16/f32 array (explicit size) a src extern declares; override-x: rejected by a reviewed entry of tools/shift/data_reloc_overrides.tsv (typed evidence, reason there); s16: s16-pair test: both halves small (|s16|<0x1000) or the value repeats >=8 times, with s16 pairs or colours around it; payload: inside what a DMA tag (dma/dma-chain) transfers: VIF codes, GIF packets, VU microcode and data; resfile: inside a relocatable resource file code fixes up with its own base (func_001763f0): offsets and numbers; script: ambiguous word in a byte stream code hands to the script VM / message parser (from that base to the next address code builds); spawn-tmpl: u16 field (+0xc..+0x20) of an object spawn template {callback, 0, n, s16/u16 x, y, w, h...} (func_001f31a8's WA); gifregs: REGS field of a GIFtag (NLOOP/FLG/NREG valid in the 8 bytes before, no register past NREG); bytes: packed bytes around it: >= 3 of the 4 neighbours have no zero byte and are not addresses, floats or ASCII (bytecode); kcode: EE code the libkernel patches copy into kernel RAM (0x80074000...) and run there: self-contained, no image address; vucode: VU microcode around it (VU nop words within 4 words); ascii: the word and its neighbours are ASCII text; colour: colour test: the value is 0x00BBGGRR with two equal channels among such words, or RGBA (alpha 0x80/0xFF/0x40/0x7F) words next to it and no pointer run; float: float test: the words around it are plausible floats, no pointer run; into-func: inside a function, not a known jump table: a number (crt0's 0x1001xx values and the like); unaligned: data/bss target not 4-aligned and not a string start; mirror-x: mirror of an address code never builds (in practice ctype/ASCII tables, 0x20202020); mipscode: MIPS instructions around it (code carried as data, e.g. 0x46A000-0x46C000); smallint: neighbours are small integers/ids and no stride evidence (counter, size, flags)
# offset: from D_BLOB = 0x00272c70; unaligned-target noise and resfile words are counted by the tool, not listed.
